observed_behavior: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.2 requires that when keyboard focus can enter a page component, users can move focus away using only a keyboard interface. If exit needs a method beyond unmodified arrow or Tab keys or other standard exit methods, the user must be advised how to exit. The accompanying non-interference note says failure may obstruct use of the whole page, including content not relied upon for conformance.
context: WCAG 2.2 W3C Recommendation, 12 December 2024; exact criterion 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap; focused W07 B1 K3 normative extraction. Level A; requirement and associated W3C notes/conditions only.
limitations: This criterion requires an available keyboard-only exit and, when applicable, exit-method instruction; it does not prohibit deliberate focus containment within a genuinely modal interaction when a keyboard exit remains available.
The criterion does not mandate a particular exit key, trap library, or an always-Tab-to-background implementation.
Non-interference note must be interpreted within WCAG conformance context; no deployed page was tested.
